who: Morihei Ueshiba · The Art of Peace, 1992
quote: Failure is the key to success; each mistake teaches us something.
meaning: Getting it wrong is how you get good. Ueshiba, born in 1883, founded aikido and saw every mistake as a lesson.

quote: I never learned anything from a match that I won; I got my golfing education from drubbings.
meaning: Bobby Jones said his wins taught him nothing and his big losses taught him golf. He won golf's Grand Slam in 1930.

quote: We learn wisdom from failure much more than from success... probably he who never made a mistake never made a discovery.
meaning: Failing teaches you more than winning. Smiles wrote in 1866 that people who never make mistakes never discover anything new.

who: José Raúl Capablanca · My Chess Career, 1920
quote: Nothing is so healthy as a thrashing at the proper time, and from few won games have I learned as much as I have from most of my defeats.
meaning: Capablanca, world chess champion from 1921, learned more from his losses than his wins, because a loss woke him up.

who: William Blake · The Marriage of Heaven and Hell, c. 1790
quote: If the fool would persist in his folly he would become wise.
meaning: Keep at it, even when it seems foolish, and the doing itself makes you wise. Blake wrote this around 1790.

who: Bernice de Pasquali · Great Singers on the Art of Singing, 1921
quote: Success in singing is at the end of a tall ladder, the rungs of which are repeated failures. We climb up over our failures to success.
meaning: Opera star de Pasquali said success is a tall ladder, and every failure is one step up it. Printed in 1921.

quote: If you shut your door to all errors truth will be shut out.
meaning: Tagore, who won the Nobel Prize in 1913, says being too afraid of mistakes also keeps the truth away.

who: Richard Feynman · The Character of Physical Law, 1965
quote: In other words we are trying to prove ourselves wrong as quickly as possible, because only in that way can we find progress.
meaning: In 1964 Feynman said scientists try to prove their own ideas wrong fast, because that is how they make progress.

who: Rabba bar Rav Huna · Talmud, Gittin 43a
quote: A person does not understand statements of Torah unless he stumbles in them.
meaning: This teacher, who died in 322, said it after taking back his own wrong ruling in public. You learn by stumbling.

who: Loie Fuller · Fifteen Years of a Dancer's Life, 1913
quote: My robe was so long that I was continually stepping upon it, and mechanically I held it up with both hands and raised my arms aloft...
meaning: Fuller kept stepping on her too-long dress, so she lifted it high. The crowd cheered. Her Serpentine Dance was born by 1891.
